overview: Somalia is a country in the Horn of Africa with the longest coastline on mainland Africa. Its capital and largest city is Mogadishu. Somalia was formed in 1960 from former British and Italian territories. Since 1991 it has been affected by civil war, and the north-west region of Somaliland has declared independence, though no country recognises it.

geography.text: Somalia's coastline runs along the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. Most of the country is dry plateau and plain, with mountains in the north. The Jubba and Shabelle rivers in the south are its only permanent rivers, and most farming takes place along them.

history.text: Somali coastal cities such as Mogadishu traded across the Indian Ocean for centuries. In the late 1800s the land was divided between Britain, Italy and France. British and Italian Somaliland united as independent Somalia in 1960. Siad Barre ruled from 1969 until 1991, when the government collapsed and civil war began.

events.title: Mogadishu
events.text: Mogadishu grows into a major trading city.

events.title: Colonial division
events.text: Britain, Italy and France divide Somali lands.

events.title: State collapse
events.text: Siad Barre is overthrown and civil war follows.

government.text: Somalia is a federal parliamentary republic rebuilding after decades of civil war. Parliament elects the President. The armed group al-Shabaab controls parts of the south. Somaliland in the north has declared independence but is not recognised by other countries.

economy.text: Livestock, especially camels, goats and sheep, is Somalia's main export. Money sent by Somalis abroad and mobile money are vital. Droughts often cause hunger.

culture.text: Somalia is often called a 'nation of poets', and oral poetry is highly respected. It has the longest coastline on mainland Africa. Somalia has more camels than any other country.

items.title: Oral poetry

items.title: Laas Geel
items.text: Cave paintings thousands of years old.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Somalia-born runner Mo Farah won four Olympic golds for Great Britain.

items.title: Mo Farah
